regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: Create the missing off-body near-wake box so the separated-shear-layer / bluff-body wake envelope is covered. Bounds are the flow_requirement:near_wake envelope padded by ~0.01 m so the float32 bounds (0.3499999940/1.0499999821/+-0.9799999833/+-0.4899999917) are strictly contained. Level 2 gives 0.04375 m, half the 0.0875 m prior (= exactly level 1), leaving a factor-2 margin for the native p95 span statistic (tolerance 1.5) instead of a knife-edge equality. Level 2 stays coarser than surface level 3, so no surface/layer/quality setting changes and the surface -> wake -> background grading is preserved. Volume 0.72*1.98*1.00 = 1.43 m^3, ~1.7e4 cells. This is an envelope prior, not a measured shear-layer thickness.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Cover the downstream velocity-deficit/shear transport envelope, padded ~0.01-0.02 m beyond the float32 bounds (1.0499999821/2.4499999583/+-1.2599999785/+-0.6299999893). The prior span 0.175 m is EXACTLY the uniform background cell (grading 1.0), so leaving it unboxed relies on an equality that any stricter native comparison or transition cell would break; level 1 = 0.0875 m supplies a factor-2 margin at ~6.9e3 cells. The upstream face overlaps the near-wake box by 0.02 m so maximum level wins and no coarse slot appears between the two envelopes. Kept deliberately at one increment (the scenario states coarser far-wake bounds cost), not refined to surface level.

advisor.hypothesis: The single configured-screen failure is a resolution-coverage failure, not a geometry or layer defect: the only off-body refinement configured is two surface-distance bands (0.04375 m -> level 3, 0.13125 m -> level 2, i.e. snappy distance shells), which cannot reach the near-wake prior envelope that extends to x = 1.05 m. Background h = 1.4/8 = 0.175 m, so level 1 = 0.0875 m and level 2 = 0.04375 m. Both scenario priors coincide EXACTLY with a native level: near_wake max span 0.0875 m == level 1, far_wake max span 0.175 m == background level 0. Configuring those exact levels therefore leaves an equality knife-edge with zero p95 headroom for the native span statistic (tolerance 1.5). Fix: two searchable boxes covering (a) the near-wake envelope of the finite cylinder (D = 0.7 m, span 1.4 m along Y, flow +X) at level 2 and (b) the far-wake envelope at level 1, each one isotropic increment finer than the prior's exact level match, modestly padded in every coordinate so the float32 requirement bounds are strictly contained. Refinement is deliberately kept BELOW the surface level 3 so the mesh still grades surface (0.021875 m) -> wake -> background and no surface/layer/quality setting changes.
advisor.expected_change: scenario_screen near_wake configured_volume_coverage 0.0 -> 1.0 and far_wake stays 1.0 (preview confirmed accepted=true); finest configured size unchanged at 0.021875 m surface, with off-body spans now <=0.04375 m inside the near-wake envelope and <=0.0875 m inside the far-wake envelope instead of 0.175 m background. Isotropic refinement increments cost ~8x cells in a fixed volume, but these envelopes are thin relative to the domain: forecast total rises 2.39e5 -> ~2.75e5 (region upper bound 23915 extra cells) against the 2e6 gate. Layer stack (8 layers, first 1.070e-3 m, ratio 1.2, stack 0.01766 m) and all quality/fidelity gates unchanged. Uncertainty: the forecast is uncalibrated and native cell count is a hard gate; the boxes are planning envelopes, not measured wake trajectories, and no CFD accuracy is claimed.
counterevidence: far_wake already screens at configured_volume_coverage 1.0 with no box at all, so refining it is numerical margin, not a stated requirement

no native mesh evidence exists yet: no layer, non-orthogonality, skewness, openness or bad-cluster failure has been measured, so no layer/snap intervention is justified
outward-ray finite hit fraction is 0.0 over 5 directional samples, but that is directional sampling only, not a proof of clearance or a medial-distance measurement
deterministic initial_certification already reports ok=true, unresolved_feature_fraction 0.0, finest 0.021875 m, so global or surface refinement has no measured defect to fix
alternatives: near wake at level 1 (exactly 0.0875 m) and no far-wake box: meets both priors only by float equality with zero p95 headroom - rejected as fragile

raise global surface_level 3 -> 4 to better sample the 64-facet cylinder tessellation (facet width 0.0344 m ~ 1.6 surface cells, sagitta 0.42 mm): rejected now because facet dihedrals are 5.6 deg, well below resolve_feature_angle 30 deg, unresolved_feature_fraction is 0.0, and it would cost ~8x near-surface cells with no measured defect

pre-emptive layer_settings change (max_thickness_to_medial_ratio, n_grow, feature_angle) for the 90 deg end-cap rims: rejected because no native extrusion/corner failure has been measured and nGrow propagates NON-EXTRUSION to neighbours rather than filling uncovered faces
one merged level-1 box over near+far wake only: rejected because it would leave the near-wake envelope at exactly the prior span with no margin
